title: IPO GMP Today Highlights| Hero Motors IPO booked nearly 1.4 times on NII push; retail portion subscribed 2.2 times - The Economic Times
text:
IPO GMP Today Highlights: NSE IPO, valued at Rs 22,561.57 crore, is set to open for subscription on September 17, 2026. The issue will remain open for investors to bid for three days.

The IPO comprises entirely an Offer for Sale (OFS), meaning the company will not receive any proceeds from the issue. After deducting their respective share of offer-related expenses and taxes, the net proceeds will accrue entirely to the Selling Shareholders.

According to Anand Rathi, Hero Motors has established a differentiated position in automotive technology, with capabilities spanning design, engineering, prototyping and manufacturing. Its product portfolio includes CVTs, EV transmissions, electric motors, drive units and gear sets, providing exposure to both internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric mobility segments.

The brokerage noted that Hero Motors has a strong presence in e-bike powertrains, while its investments in Hewland and its joint venture with Yamaha Motor Japan further strengthen its transmission and electric motor capabilities. With operations across India, the UK and Thailand, the company has developed a global operating footprint.

At the upper end of the IPO price band, Hero Motors is valued at a P/E multiple of 92.6x and an EV/EBITDA multiple of 34.38x based on FY26 earnings. The company's post-issue market capitalisation is estimated at Rs 38,154 million. Anand Rathi said the IPO appears fully priced but assigned a “Subscribe – Long Term” rating to the issue.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has reduced the size of its proposed initial public offering (IPO) offer for sale (OFS) by around 15%, with several shareholders trimming the number of shares they plan to sell, according to the red herring prospectus (RHP) filed on September 10.

The total OFS has been cut to up to 12.64 crore shares, from 14.89 crore shares proposed in the updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP). This represents a reduction of approximately 2.25 crore shares.

The entire reduction has come from eight selling shareholders. MS Strategic (Mauritius) has lowered its proposed sale by 0.50 crore shares, while Stock Holding Corporation of India has reduced its offer by 0.47 crore shares.

General Insurance Corporation of India has cut its proposed sale by 0.45 crore shares, followed by Bank of Baroda, which has reduced its offer by 0.33 crore shares. National Insurance Company has trimmed its proposed sale by 0.20 crore shares.

Retail investors have been allotted 35% of the issue, while 50% is reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). The remaining shares have been earmarked for non-institutional investors (NIIs).

At the upper end of the price band, the NSE IPO will command a valuation of Rs 22,561.57 crore, making it the second-largest IPO in India’s history. At this valuation, NSE’s market capitalisation will stand at around Rs 4.41 lakh crore.

Eligible employees participating in the issue will also benefit from a Rs 170-per-share discount.

The much-awaited Hero Motors IPO opened for subscription on September 16, 2026, marking the start of its three-day bidding period. The issue will remain open for investors until September 18. Meanwhile, the IPO is attracting strong interest in the grey market, where its shares are currently commanding a 23% premium, pointing to expectations of a potentially strong listing if the current trend continues.
